Roofing Automation

What Happens When a Roofing AI Assistant Doesn't Know the Answer?

Roofing Automation

An AI assistant is only given approved information to work with — common questions, scheduling logic, and qualification questions your team has signed off on. When a homeowner asks something outside that scope — a technical roofing question, a pricing edge case, or anything requiring judgment — the assistant is designed to recognize that and hand the conversation to a person, rather than guess.

Why this matters

A confidently wrong answer about roofing materials, timelines, or pricing can cost more trust than a slower but accurate one. The assistant's boundaries are defined deliberately — it operates within an approved question-and-answer scope, and anything outside that scope is treated as an escalation, not a guess.

What escalation actually looks like

The conversation is flagged for a team member, with the context already captured — what the homeowner asked, what's already been discussed, and any information collected so far. The homeowner isn't left without a response; they're told a team member will follow up, and that handoff is logged in your CRM so nothing gets lost between the automated and human parts of the conversation.

Setting the boundary correctly

This requires deciding upfront which questions are safe for the assistant to answer and which should always go to a person — for example, general scheduling and common FAQs versus anything about roof condition, safety, or final pricing. Getting that boundary right is part of setting the system up, not something left to chance.

This escalation behavior is built into 2S's roofing AI assistant setup.
